name: Zwiesel
prior: Sampled two-tone bells exist on tablet and desktop: Kong Audio 'Bian Zhong' / 'Bian Zhong Pro' (Windows VST, 88 bells recorded at the HuBei Chime-bells Orchestra, 'one bell with two tones', USD 129; VS: kvraudio.com/news/29235; adorama.com/kabianzhongp.html) and Kong Audio 'BianZhong BZ Bells' for iPad (2015; VS: apps.apple.com/app/id956078325; rekkerd.org 'kong-audio-releases-bianzhong-bz-bells-app-ipad'); Sound Magic BianZhong virtual instrument (VS: bigbearsound.com). Synthesis research: NYCU thesis 'Sound Synthesis Model of Chinese Chime-Bells Based on Inharmonic Digital Waveguides' (sampled a Zeng Hou Yi replica set, two models; VS: ir.lib.nycu.edu.tw/handle/11536/46613); Weijia Yang 2025 'A Novel Physical Modeling Approach for Sound Synthesis of Chinese Chime Bells' with GitHub code (VS: protocols.io); 'Digital and physical re-creation of ancient Chinese bells' 2024 (replica pair with A-tones D5 and B-tones E5/F5, i.e. seconds, not thirds; VS: nature.com/articles/s41599-024-04133-8). Physics: Rossing & Zhu 1989 on ten Shanghai Museum bells - ratio of the two (2,0) fundamentals 1.11-1.31 (181-473 cents), (3,0) pairs at 2.32-3.29 times the lowest (2,0) (VS: labs.sonicfield.org summary of JASA 1989, citing JASA 83, 369 (1988)); 'the interval between the two tones usually ranges from a major third to a minor third', each circular mode becomes an a/b doublet (VS: acoustics.org/pressroom 133rd 2pmu1, 138th rossing1); modern peace bell doublets differ 3-10 % (VS: researchgate 256799292); A-tone = strike at the centre of the face near the rim, B-tone at the side (VS: music.si.edu/node/179); R: synthesis.md 3.4. Mainstream modal synths (Chromaphone, Rings modal, Reason Resonans, 2hp Bell) have no strike-point two-tone object (VS: sonicstate 2017; analoguehaven 2hp bell manual; R: synthesis.md section 5). Not found: a synthesized two-tone bell with the strike point under the finger and the B-tone snapped to the scale.
costNotes: O path = Saite class: 1 BufferSource + lowpass + 8 ms click noise = ~0.3-0.35 at L1 (Saite is 0.35, APP 2081), L3 two bells 0.7. N path: 6 oscillators + 6 gains + lowpass + click = ~16 nodes = 6x0.06 + 8x0.03 + 0.06 + 0.1 = ~0.75 (Glocke's 0.7 for ~10 nodes calibrates this), L3 with 8 oscillators per side ~1.6 - the idea's 1.3 / 2.4 is pessimistic. The real cost of the O path is memory, not CPU: nachklang 5 s x 48 kHz x 4 B = 0.96 MB per buffer (2.3 MB at 12 s), times 5 strike points times 11-15 field notes = 53-72 MB per setting, against the KS cache cap of 1e7 frames / 80 entries (APP ksStore) -> permanent thrashing and synchronous first renders. Fix: the model is linear, so render three group buffers per note (A doublet, B doublet, shared modes) once and mix them at play with gains w_A, w_B, w_S -> y continuous, 3 BufferSources (+0.1 units), 3 x 3 s per note (the exponential tail continued natively via setTargetAtTime) = ~1.7 MB per note, 20-26 MB for a field. Alternative with continuous everything: a worklet modal bank (16 resonators measured 0.61 units, R: webaudio.md section 4) with strike-point gains as k-rate params - more CPU, no cache.
soundHeld: Struck engine: the hold is the decay; the strike point under the finger (y) picks A, B or both and the shared doublets beat between them - the dyad-from-one-object and the Wirbel 'Terz-Tremolo' (roll while moving y) are real new gestures with no counterpart in Glocke (FM) or Schale. Two things must change for it to sound like bronze rather than 'Glocke mit Terz': (1) the partial table is a Western handbell (Csound 1, 1.0019, 1.794, 1.801, 2.52, 2.99, 3.79; R: synthesis.md 2.9) - a bianzhong has (3,0) at 2.32-3.29 x (2,0)a and a/b splits of 3-10 % in the upper doublets (VS), so build the table from Rossing's ranges (A: 1, 1.004; B = 1.19-1.26 x A with its own doublet; (3,0) pair 2.4/2.9; (4,0) 3.9/4.6 ...), with decays T60 proportional to 1/sqrt(f) and a hard-mallet click; (2) the beat rates: 'schwebung 0-8 ct' is 0-2 Hz at 440 Hz (gentle, Schale-like), real bells beat 3-10 % = 13-44 Hz (roughness) - put the gentle doublets on the hum pair and a rougher split on one upper pair so the bronze has grain. 'spalt = terz' as 'next scale note >= 2 steps above' breaks on Myzel's pentatonic scales (APP 1638): Dur-Pentatonik gives a major third only from the root and fourths (500 ct) from the other four degrees, Moll-Pentatonik gives fourths from all five, Hirajoshi a tritone from one degree - outside the 181-473 ct a bell can do; choose instead the scale note nearest 350 ct above (window 180-480 ct), else a free 350 ct. playbackRate transposition halves/doubles decay and beat rates within the +-1-octave neighbour search (accepted, like Saite).
soundBurst: Puls: a hit with bright = strike point -> a lane plays A, B or the dyad from one note, with decayMul and gate as Glocke; Sporenregen-ready like Glocke/Schale (RG_S). With 5 quantised strike points a rolled finger or a modulated 'bright' jumps between tones audibly; with the three-group mix y is continuous and the Terz-Tremolo works. First notes after a scale change render synchronously unless warmed like warmKS (the same per-layer/lane note set, times 3 groups instead of 5 points).
failureModes: 'terz' snapping picks fourths on both pentatonic scales (4 of 5 or 5 of 5 degrees) and a tritone in Hirajoshi: use the scale note nearest 350 ct (180-480 ct window) or a free 350 ct
O cache: 5 strike points x notes x 1-2.3 MB = 50-70 MB per setting, thrashing the 40 MB / 80-entry cap: render three group buffers per note and mix by gain
Quantised strike points make y jumps audible under a roll; the dyad weights must be continuous
Handbell partial table is Western: bianzhong needs (3,0) at 2.3-3.3 x (2,0)a and rougher upper doublets, else it reads as 'Glocke mit Terz'
Gentle 0-2 Hz doublets sound like Schale; keep one rough pair (10-30 Hz) for bronze grain
Sampled bianzhong exists on iPad and Windows (Kong Audio): the claim must be 'synthesized, strike point under the finger, in the scale', not 'two-tone bell'
playbackRate reuse changes decay and beat rate (x2 per octave): keep the neighbour search to +-1 octave, not 2
verdict: Rare: two-tone bells are sold sampled (Kong Audio Bian Zhong Pro on Windows, BZ Bells on iPad) and modelled in theses (NYCU inharmonic waveguides, Yang 2025), but no synth puts the strike point of a two-tone object under a finger with the second tone snapped to the scale, and mainstream modal synths have no such object. Native and cheap: the offline-buffer path is Saite-class (~0.35 units, L3 ~0.7; the N path ~0.75, not 1.3) - the real cost is the cache, which at 5 strike points x notes x 1-2 MB thrashes the 40 MB cap and must become three group buffers per note mixed by gain, which also makes the strike point continuous. Musically the dyad-from-one-hit and the Wirbel Terz-Tremolo are genuinely new gestures and Puls lanes playing thirds from one note are attractive, provided the 'terz' rule is fixed (on Myzel's pentatonic scales it yields fourths and a tritone, outside the 181-473 ct a bell can do) and the partial table is rebuilt from Rossing's bianzhong data instead of the Western handbell, otherwise it is heard as 'Glocke mit Terz'.
